heading: INT. FOOD TRUCK - "BIG DAVE'S BAPS" - MORNING

units.text: INT. FOOD TRUCK - "BIG DAVE'S BAPS" - MORNING
A grey Tuesday, drizzle on the awning.
The griddle ticks as it warms.
Condensation on every surface.
Somewhere outside, a gull has opinions.
MO, 40s, in a stained apron and a flat cap, cracks eggs one-handed, humming something tuneless.
The queue outside, five or six commuters under umbrellas, shuffles forward.
His mobile buzzes on the counter.
He wipes his hand on his apron and answers on speaker.
Morning. Bap's Place. Go on.
units.name: MO

units.text: This is an automated message from Harbour Borough Council Environmental Health. Your inspection for today has been brought forward. An officer will arrive at your location in approximately two minutes.
units.name: RECORDED VOICE

units.text: Mo stares at the phone.
A pause.
The kettle, left to its own devices, begins to whistle.
Right. Lovely. Marvellous.
units.name: MO

units.text: He turns the griddle off, then on, then off again.
He sweeps a tray of something suspiciously orange into the bin and hides the bin behind the fridge.
Through the hatch, a man in a hi-vis jacket with a clipboard is crossing the car park, and the queue sees him too.
The queue scatters.
Mo and the kettle both freeze.
Rain.
A single gull lands on the awning.
Not ideal.
units.name: MO
